title: What happened to the Neanderthals?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore what happened to the Neanderthals. They cover the 1856 discovery in the Neander Valley near Dusseldorf and early racist-era interpretations of Neanderthals as brutes, the species split from a common Heidelbergensis ancestor in Africa, Neanderthal range across Eurasia, and the overlap with Homo sapiens after sapiens reached the Middle East and Europe. They contrast the replacement model with the multiregional/interbreeding view, citing Neanderthal DNA in modern non-African people and a 2019 French fertility-decline study tied to climate. The hosts then discuss evidence that Neanderthals were behaviorally modern: tool making (Levallois technique), fire, big-game hunting, body adornment, cave art dated by uranium-thorium methods, possible bone flutes, deliberate burials with flowers, care for disabled individuals, and possible language. The episode also includes a mid-episode ad read, a Geico reference, and a long listener mail segment.
topics: stuff you should know listener mail

segments.title: Opening banter and pronunciation
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the topic and debate how to pronounce Neanderthal (Neander Tal vs. Neanderthal).

segments.title: Discovery of Neanderthal fossils
segments.summary: Early fossil finds in Belgium and Gibraltar, then the 1856 discovery in the Neander Valley near Dusseldorf, where Fuhlrott and Schaaffhausen recognized a distinct human species. The name Homo neanderthalensis is explained.

segments.title: Racist science and early views of Neanderthals
segments.summary: Discussion of how the discovery came before Darwin's ideas were widely accepted and how phrenology and racist science shaped the caveman stereotype of Neanderthals as brutes.

segments.title: Origins and range of Neanderthals
segments.summary: Neanderthals and Homo sapiens split from a common Heidelbergensis ancestor in Africa, with Neanderthals becoming a distinct species by about 400,000 years ago. Their range covered Eurasia from Portugal and Wales to Siberia and the Middle East, with populations waxing and waning over time.

segments.title: Sapiens and Neanderthals overlap, then disappearance
segments.summary: Homo sapiens reached the Middle East about 100,000 years ago and shared Europe with Neanderthals for roughly 200 to 500 generations before Neanderthals vanished around 40,000 years ago.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode ad break for the show's sponsor.

segments.title: Replacement model vs. interbreeding
segments.summary: The replacement model (sapiens outcompeted or killed off Neanderthals) is contrasted with the multiregional model, supported by the 2010 Neanderthal genome sequencing showing that many non-African people carry 1 to 4 percent Neanderthal DNA. A 2019 French study suggests a small fertility decline driven by climate could have caused the gradual disappearance.

segments.title: Neanderthal appearance, disease and tool making
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the rehabilitated image of Neanderthals as not hunched and possibly with red hair and pale skin, the William movie, possible disease links to Neanderthal DNA, and the Levallois technique of pre-shaping stone tools.

segments.title: Behavioral modernity: fire, hunting, art, and burial
segments.summary: Evidence that Neanderthals made fire, hunted large game at close range, used body adornment and pigments, made cave art dated by uranium-thorium methods to over 64,000 years ago, possibly made bone flutes, and buried their dead with flowers. Copying arguments against Neanderthal symbolism are mentioned.

segments.title: Neanderthal care for others and language
segments.summary: Evidence of a disabled Neanderthal who lived into his forties with community support, and Dutch researchers' argument that Neanderthals likely spoke a modern-style language.

segments.title: Geico caveman and Smithsonian exhibit
segments.summary: Light discussion of the Geico caveman parody and a Smithsonian Neanderthal skeleton exhibit.

segments.title: Administrative and listener mail
segments.summary: Thanks to listeners for gifts including Crown Royal glasses, a Twinkie the Kid statue, Wendy's chili, miso, beer chocolates, pens, dog collars, and other items. Sign-off with contact info.
